misconceptions.description: Treating any frame of bars as an ideal truss
misconceptions.trigger: learner labels a structure as a truss without considering joint loading and pin assumptions
misconceptions.feedback: A truss in introductory statics is idealized as straight members connected by pins with loads applied at joints, so not every bar framework qualifies under the same assumptions.

misconceptions.description: Thinking triangular layouts are just a stylistic choice
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats the triangle pattern as decorative rather than structural
misconceptions.feedback: Triangles matter because they preserve geometry under load and help route axial forces efficiently through the structure.

misconceptions.description: Interpreting a negative member-force result as a math failure
misconceptions.trigger: learner rejects a negative method-of-joints result
misconceptions.feedback: With a tension-first convention, a negative member-force result usually means the member is actually in compression.
